Definition: a village (as covered in by walls); also a young lion (perhaps as covered with a mane)
BiblicalUsage: Kephiyr means a village, and also a young lion: Nehemiah 6:2 says Sanballat sent, come, let us meet together in some one of the villages in the plain of Ono, but they thought to do me mischief. Isaiah 11:6 says the calf and the young lion and the fatling together, and a little child shall lead them. Amos 3:4 asks, will a young lion cry out of his den, if he have taken nothing? Zechariah 11:3 says there is a voice of the roaring of young lions, for the pride of Jordan is spoiled.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the young lion is two pictures at once: the predator that roars when it has prey, and the cub that lies down with the lamb when the child leads. I hold that the villages of Ono were a trap, and the peace of Isaiah is the promise that the trap is not the end.
RelatedPeople: Nehemiah; Isaiah; Amos; Zechariah the Prophet
